title: Stochastic sensitivity engine for reach-impact-cost-effort roadmap scoring
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Deliver a lightweight, reproducible simulator that extends Reach-Impact-Cost-Effort (RICE) style scoring into a stochastic, sensitivity-aware prioritization output for roadmap planning and OKR tradeoffs.

Problem: Deterministic RICE scores hide uncertainty and can lead to brittle roadmap choices when cost or latency estimates are noisy. Teams at Redwood need a way to: (1) quantify ranking stability under estimate variance, (2) visualize trade-offs between latency/cost and product impact, and (3) feed uncertainty-aware priorities into cycle planning and rollout decisions.

Proposed solution: Build a simulator service + interactive dashboard that: 
- Accepts candidate initiatives with distributions for Reach, Impact, Confidence, Cost, and Latency (e.g., mean+stdev or percentiles).
- Runs Monte Carlo sampling to produce posterior distributions of RICE-style scores and rank-order probabilities (P(rank=1), P(in top-3), etc.).
- Computes sensitivity and elasticity metrics: how much a % change in cost or latency changes expected rank or expected value.
- Produces scenario views for OKR alignment: optimistic, base, pessimistic; and multi-objective filters (minimize latency increases while maximizing OKR coverage).
- Exposes an API for cycle planners to pull prioritized lists with confidence bands and a small payload for Redwood Console to display per-route risk and suggested mitigations (e.g., canary gating, deferred quantization).

Success criteria: 
- Roadmap planners can identify initiatives with >80% rank stability across plausible estimate ranges.
- Reduction in post-rollout surprises where priority reversal is later attributed to estimate variance.
- Adoption by at least two PM teams in Cycle 42 for actual prioritization runs.

Implementation notes / scope: 
- Phase 1 (MVP): web-based simulator + CSV import/ export + basic dashboard for rank probability and sensitivity table. No RBAC or cross-account sharing.
- Phase 2: API hooks, Console integration, per-initiative historical estimate tracking, and export to Linear backlog.
- Phase 3: coupling with Optimize recommendations (cost/quantization suggestions) and runtime telemetry to refine priors.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Full Bayesian model gives richer posteriors but requires more data and infra; we start with Monte Carlo using user-specified priors to be pragmatic.
- Keeping UX lightweight vs. exposing many knobs: initial UI will prioritize common default distributions (normal/log-normal/two-point optimistic/pessimistic) with an "advanced" toggle.

Artifacts: 
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/PM-47589+-+Stochastic+Sensitivity+Engine (draft)

comments: 2025-01-07 - Maya Chen: Kickoff meeting notes attached in Confluence. Agreed MVP scope = CSV import + single-cycle simulation + rank probability table. Action: ENG spike to validate sampling performance on 200 candidates.

2025-01-15 - Aisha Patel: ENG spike complete. Sampling 10k draws for 200 candidates finishes in ~1.2s on a single provisioned pod using vectorized numpy. Raised question about deterministic seeding for reproducibility.

2025-01-22 - Daniel Ortega (Engineering lead): Reviewed tradeoffs in architecture. Recommend a lightweight Python service with optional Rust core if perf becomes a bottleneck. Will open ENG task to prototype API: ENG-3128.

2025-01-28 - Product review: PM and Design feedback - add 'OKR coverage' dimension so scoring can be weighted by strategic fit. Design requested a compact sparkline for rank volatility next to each initiative in the dashboard.

2025-02-03 - Aisha Patel: Prototype dashboard v0 deployed to staging. Screenshot link: https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/pm-47589/dashboard-v0.png. Initial feedback: add tooltips explaining sensitivity metrics (elasticity = pct rank change / pct cost change).

2025-02-09 - Maya Chen: Went through a prioritization dry-run with Growth and Core infra PMs. Two takeaways: (1) teams want an export that writes back prioritized order to Linear as 'priority' tag, (2) prefer default prior for latency to be log-normal to avoid negative samples. Filed follow-up sub-issue PM-47590 for Linear export.
2025-02-12 - Design review: UX approval pending microcopy for uncertainty explanations. Designer assigned: Javier Ruiz. Next: schedule user testing with 3 PMs during Cycle planning week.
